method: Source-of-record check at authoring time, then a separate second pass re-reading every numeric and quoted claim against the page it came from. Author and checker are the same pass, which is not the independent arrangement the older batches used.

findings.claim: Global median C:P, N:P and C:N ratios of 163, 22 and 6.6, with extensive regional variation
Redfield identified a mean marine C:N:P of 106:16:1 and matched it to deep-ocean nitrate and phosphate
Ratios exceed Redfield proportions in subtropical regions and fall below them in high-latitude and equatorial upwelling regions
Phosphorus is used disproportionately in ribosomes, so fast growth is phosphorus-hungry
findings.sourceChecked: standard cell biology; not quoted from a source read in this pass
findings.note: Offered as the mechanism behind the regional pattern, written without a figure and without attribution to a specific study.

findings.claim: Wood holds very little nitrogen or phosphorus, so forests accumulate carbon at a low nutrient cost until supply binds
findings.note: Carried from existing verified material rather than re-sourced.

findings.claim: Ammonia production accounts for around 2% of total final energy consumption and 1.3% of CO2 emissions from the energy system
Around 70% of ammonia is used to make fertilisers
Around 180 million tonnes of ammonia are made each year
findings.note: The figure is widely cited but does not appear on the page we read. The sentence now says the output is industrial-scale and overwhelmingly fertiliser, with no tonnage.

findings.claim: The nitrogenase reaction is N2 + 8H+ + 8e- + 16 MgATP -> 2NH3 + H2 + 16 MgADP + 16 Pi, and both processes are energy consumptive
Nitrogenase proteins are oxygen sensitive and must be handled anaerobically
Most ammonia hydrogen comes from steam methane reforming, whose CO2 is a product of the chemistry rather than of combustion
findings.sourceChecked: process description; the IEA page read here gives the totals rather than the route split
findings.note: Stated as a description of the process with no share attached to it.

findings.claim: The stoichiometry: 16 MgATP, 8 electrons and 8 protons per N2, producing 2 NH3 and one H2
Nitrogenase is markedly oxygen sensitive and must be worked with anaerobically
16 ATP at ~50 kJ/mol of hydrolysis is roughly 800 kJ per mole of N2
findings.sourceChecked: arithmetic, using the hydrolysis figure from https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12256841/
findings.note: Our conversion, combining two sources; stated as approximate.

findings.claim: The extra two electrons are mechanistically obligatory rather than a catalytic inefficiency
findings.note: The H2 appears in the balanced equation the paper gives; the word 'obligatory' is our reading and is hedged as 'thought to be'.

findings.claim: Heterocysts, slime layers, temporal separation and leghaemoglobin-containing nodules are the routes around oxygen sensitivity
findings.sourceChecked: standard microbiology; not quoted from a source read in this pass

findings.claim: Excess nitrogen and phosphorus cause algal blooms; agriculture and stormwater are key contributors
Phosphorus is a common constituent of fertilisers, manure and organic wastes; soil and bank erosion are major contributors to streams
Excess phosphorus speeds eutrophication; algal overgrowth decreases dissolved oxygen as algae decay, leaving dead zones
The United States is the world's leading producer and consumer of phosphate rock
Phosphate rock production and reserve figures by country
findings.note: The overview page carries no figures; they live in linked commodity summaries we did not open. No production or reserve numbers are given in the article.

findings.claim: Phosphorus has no significant atmospheric reservoir and no biological fixation route
findings.sourceChecked: the absence of a gas phase; contrasted against the nitrogenase reaction in PMC10100503
findings.note: A structural statement rather than a quoted one; the contrast with nitrogen is sourced.

findings.claim: Legacy phosphorus in soils and lake sediments delays recovery after inputs fall
findings.note: Carried from an existing verified article.

findings.claim: A depletion zone of nutrients develops rapidly around roots, and hyphae extend beyond it to mobilise phosphate from regions roots cannot reach
Up to 22% of photosynthetically fixed carbon is traded for symbiotic phosphate
In tomato and flax the mycorrhizal pathway contributed 100% of phosphate acquired; in rice AMF contributes up to 70%
Hyphae are one to two orders of magnitude thinner than roots
findings.sourceChecked: not quoted from a source read in this pass
findings.note: Stated as the geometric reason for the advantage; approximate and unattributed.

findings.claim: Colonisation is suppressed where soil phosphate is abundant
findings.note: Consistent with the review's framing of a cost-benefit exchange; written without a figure.

findings.claim: Soil erosion is a major contributor of phosphorus to streams, including bank erosion during floods
Agriculture and stormwater are key contributors of excess nutrients; blooms release toxins that can make people and animals sick
Ammonia production accounts for around 2% of total final energy consumption
Nitrate leaves in drainage and as gas; phosphorus leaves attached to particles in storms
findings.sourceChecked: corpus cross-reference: content/en/ecology/soils/nutrient-availability-and-soil-fertility.md, already verified, plus the USGS erosion statement
findings.note: The loss-pathway table in the existing verified article carries the same split; no new figures are introduced here.

findings.claim: No-till can increase preferential flow of nitrate through macropores
findings.note: Stated as a possible negative effect with 'sometimes', not as a general finding, because we did not read a source establishing it.
